clue.text: Underwear trimmed in Silver?

indicators.note: trimmed means the underwear's name is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: long johns are long-legged woollen underpants

explanation.surface: A question about a pair of underpants cut down and edged in silver thread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silver' with a capital and a query is the pirate Long John Silver of Treasure Island, a definition by example; 'trimmed' cuts the S off the underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-legged pirate of Stevenson's Treasure Island is known by these forenames, with Silver his surname.

clue.text: Subordinate who founded The Threepenny Review

definitions.meaning: lower in rank or importance; a minor or inferior one
Wendy ... founded the Berkeley literary magazine The Threepenny Review in 1980

explanation.definitionFit: A lesser thing is a minor one, and the editor Wendy Lesser founded the Berkeley literary quarterly.

clue.text: Work Sartre couldn't get out of?

definitions.text: Work Sartre couldn't get out of?

parts.words: Work Sartre couldn't get out of?
parts.note: a play by Sartre in which three characters are locked in a room in hell that none can leave, read as a work that offers its author no way out

explanation.definitionFit: Sartre's play Huis Clos, about three souls trapped in a room in hell, is known in English by this title.

clue.text: Agent preserves agreement to secure energy

indicators.note: to secure means the preserves hold the energy letter inside them

parts.note: fruit preserves are jams
E is the symbol for energy in physics
a bond is a binding agreement

explanation.surface: An agent keeps a deal going so as to lock in power supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'preserves' looks like a verb, 'keeps', but it is the noun JAMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ian Fleming's secret agent 007 is the most famous fictional spy.

clue.text: Hornby book, welcome delight, if surprisingly unknown

parts.note: hi is a word of welcome

indicators.note: surprisingly means the letters come out in an unexpected arrangement

parts.note: y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A welcome pleasure for a Nick Hornby reader, if it arrives by surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' turns DELIGHTIF into GHFIDELIT. Nick Hornby is an English novelist; 'Hornby' might also suggest the model-railway maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick Hornby's 1995 novel about a record-shop owner carries this title.

clue.text: Stark railway for soldier returning from West

parts.note: stark means bald, as in the bald or stark facts

explanation.surface: A bleak railway line set aside for a soldier coming home from the western front.
explanation.walkthrough: Rebecca West's novel The Return of the Soldier is about Captain Chris Baldry coming home shell-shocked from the war, so 'returning from West' is literary: the soldier in West's book, not a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Chris, the shell-shocked captain in Rebecca West's 1918 novel The Return of the Soldier, bears this surname.

clue.text: Arcadian king a girl left upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the girl and left are turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A king of Arcadia upset a young woman and walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SUE plus L into LEUS, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleus was a mythical king of Tegea in Arcadia, father of Auge.

clue.text: Morrison novel unfeeling about a successful high-flyer

indicators.note: about means the whole run of letters is turned round and read the other way

parts.note: Sula is a 1973 novel by Toni Morrison
dead means numb or without feeling

explanation.surface: A Toni Morrison novel, cold about a high achiever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns SULADEAD backwards. Icarus flew too near the sun and fell; his father Daedalus flew on, hence 'successful'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the craftsman made wings of feathers and wax and escaped Crete, unlike his son, who fell.

clue.text: Architect, Minoru, turning up a month before Munro?

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means a month is read bottom to top

parts.note: May is a month
Saki was the pen name of the writer Hector Hugh Munro

explanation.surface: A Japanese architect has a month off before the hill-climbing season in the Scottish Munros.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' turns A MAY into YAMA; 'before' is a link. A Munro is also a Scottish mountain, hence the query.
explanation.definitionFit: Minoru Yamasaki was the Japanese-American architect who designed the World Trade Center towers.

clue.text: Wise crew has cut early train times

indicators.note: the crew has cut into the wise word, so one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: wise means sage
a crew is a team

explanation.surface: A clever rail crew has trimmed the timetable for the early trains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wise' may suggest the comedian Ernie Wise, but it is simply the adjective SAGE, which TEAM cuts into.
explanation.definitionFit: The era of steam locomotives was the early period of railway history.

clue.text: Monotony with not one but Stainer's sixth hymn

indicators.note: not one but another letter means the I in the dull word gives way to a new letter

parts.note: monotony is tedium
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: Stainer's sixth means the sixth letter of the name Stainer

explanation.surface: A dull composition by the Victorian composer Sir John Stainer, his sixth hymn tune.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the I of TEDIUM for E, the sixth letter of Stainer; 'with' and 'but' are links. John Stainer was an English church composer, so the surface sits neatly in the hymnbook.
explanation.definitionFit: The Te Deum is an ancient Latin hymn of praise sung at Matins.

clue.text: Press broadcast into the open land

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard rather than read, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to come forth is to come out into the open
an estate is a tract of land

explanation.surface: The press sends its broadcasts out across open country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' looks like part of the media picture with 'Press', but it signals that FORTH is to be heard, giving the same-sounding FOURTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalists collectively are called the fourth estate, after the three traditional estates of the realm.

clue.text: Hophni's dad's hosting a prophet

indicators.note: the father's name is hosting, so it holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: Hophni and Phinehas were the sons of the priest Eli in the Book of Samuel, so his father's is ELI'S

explanation.surface: The father of the biblical Hophni entertains a prophet in his home.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'dad's' supplies the S, so ELIS holds A.
explanation.definitionFit: Elias is the Greek form of Elijah, the Old Testament prophet, as in the New Testament.

clue.text: Yorick's skull covers paper with soil, not oil

parts.note: a traditional large size of writing paper, about thirteen by eight inches

indicators.note: soil not oil means the letters of oil are taken away from soil

parts.note: the word oil gives its own three letters to remove

explanation.surface: A gravedigger's picture: Yorick's skull wrapped in paper and earth rather than oil.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorick is the dead jester in Hamlet, so what covered his skull were a jester's caps; the paper size is named after the jester's-cap watermark. Soil without OIL leaves S.
explanation.definitionFit: A jester wore a belled cap on his head, and Yorick was the king's jester whose skull Hamlet holds.

clue.text: In awe of work's curt end after meandering

indicators.note: after meandering means once the letters have wandered about they settle in a new order

parts.note: taken as the letters of works, with the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone humbled by the abrupt ending of a rambling piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link. Brian Selznick's novel Wonderstruck gives a literary flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: To be filled with amazement and admiration is to be full of wonder.

clue.text: Article of sharp fruit Romeo's raised in a play

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means one letter is lifted higher up the word

parts.note: citric describes the sharp acid taste of lemons and limes
R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Something to do with lemons and Romeo turning up in a stage play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' moves the R of CITRIC up the word, giving CRITIC. Sheridan's 1779 comedy satirises theatre reviewers.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Brinsley Sheridan's 1779 burlesque about a rehearsal and its reviewers is a well-known play.

clue.text: Dismiss a charlatan, not the whole tribe

indicators.note: not the whole means only part of the run of words is used, a stretch held inside them

explanation.surface: Throw out a fraud, but not the entire tribe with him.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'Dismiss' into 'charlatan'.
explanation.definitionFit: Issachar was one of the twelve tribes of Israel, descended from Jacob's ninth son.

clue.text: Borrow book — a novel crazy about Greece

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the abbreviation
crazy means the letters of a novel go wild and rearrange

parts.note: GR is the international code for Greece

explanation.surface: Borrow a book, a crazy novel about Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: George Borrow was a Victorian travel writer; 'Borrow' is not a verb. 'crazy' turns A NOVEL into LAVENO, which goes 'about' GR.
explanation.definitionFit: George Borrow's 1851 semi-autobiographical novel about gypsies has this Romani title.

clue.text: Scurrilous paper survey she dealt out

parts.note: to survey a page is to scan it

indicators.note: dealt out like cards, the letters are distributed into a new order

explanation.surface: A gossip rag runs a poll that a woman handed round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dealt out' reads as one phrase, but 'dealt' is fodder with 'she' and 'out' alone signals the anagram, giving DALSHEET.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabloid trading in gossip and malicious rumour is known by this name.

clue.text: Play husband with charm, not upper-class

indicators.note: not upper-class means the letter for upper-class is dropped from the charm

parts.note: an amulet is a charm worn against evil
U means upper-class, from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U

explanation.surface: Flirt with a husband using one's charm, though not a posh one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like a verb (flirt), but it is the noun, Shakespeare's tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragedy of the Prince of Denmark is among the best-known stage plays.

clue.text: Footballer, with American dad, whose Achilles became vulnerable

parts.note: Pele was the great Brazilian footballer
US means American

explanation.surface: A footballer with an American father whose Achilles tendon gave way.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an Achilles tendon injury; the definition is mythical: Achilles' heel was vulnerable because his mother held him there when dipping him in the Styx.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the king of the Myrmidons married Thetis and fathered Achilles.

clue.text: Shakespearian cynic, missing link to Ursula, sombre initially

parts.note: the missing link is the supposed half-ape, half-human ancestor, an apeman

indicators.note: initially means the first letters of the three following words are taken

explanation.surface: A cynical character who has lost touch with a gloomy woman called Ursula.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing link' looks like 'lacking a connection' but is the evolutionary apeman.
explanation.definitionFit: Apemantus is the churlish philosopher in Timon of Athens who sneers at Timon's flatterers.

clue.text: Walker maybe beginning to attract insects

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: lice are small parasitic insects

explanation.surface: A hiker may start drawing bugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Alice Walker is the American author of The Color Purple; 'maybe' marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Alice is the first name of the novelist Walker, author of The Color Purple.

clue.text: Magdalen fellow who wrote and studied English

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university

explanation.surface: An Oxford don at Magdalen College who wrote books and read English.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Reade, author of The Cloister and the Hearth, held a fellowship at Magdalen College, Oxford, for most of his life; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian novelist Charles Reade was elected a fellow of Magdalen College, Oxford, and kept the post for life.

clue.text: Witch to free a chap from Hogwarts

parts.note: a hag is an ugly old witch
to rid is to free of something

explanation.surface: A witch sets out to liberate a boy from the wizarding school in the Harry Potter books.
explanation.walkthrough: Hogwarts is the school of wizardry in the Harry Potter books; its half-giant gamekeeper is the chap meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubeus, the half-giant gamekeeper at the wizarding school in Rowling's books, bears this surname.

clue.text: Swift Tom, a US author, taking the lead as a cowardly knight

parts.note: swift means fast

indicators.note: taking the lead means the leading letter is taken away from the author's name

parts.note: Tom Wolfe was the American author of The Bonfire of the Vanities

explanation.surface: A speedy American writer called Tom pushes to the front, though in fact he is a knight who runs away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swift' suggests Jonathan Swift, but it is just FAST; 'taking the lead' sounds like going first but removes W from WOLFE.
explanation.definitionFit: In Henry VI Part One, Sir John Fastolfe flees the battle and is stripped of his Garter for cowardice.

clue.text: Mayo novelist I introduced to Arundhati?

indicators.note: introduced to means put into the middle of the following name

parts.note: Arundhati Roy is the Indian author of The God of Small Things
I is one, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: An Irish novelist presents herself to the Booker winner from India.
explanation.walkthrough: Sally Rooney, author of Normal People, comes from Castlebar in County Mayo, Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Sally Rooney, author of Normal People and Conversations with Friends, was born and raised in Castlebar, County Mayo.

clue.text: Mark Antony's friend died with a secret unexpectedly

indicators.note: unexpectedly means the letters turn up in an order nobody expected

explanation.surface: A friend of Mark Antony dies holding a secret no one saw coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' turns A SECRET into ERCETAS after D.
explanation.definitionFit: Dercetas is one of Antony's followers in Antony and Cleopatra, who brings his sword to Caesar after his death.
